answer: Forging N identities costs N times the bond and N times the interaction history, which grows expensive fast. Sybil resistance here works by tying each agent identity to a bonded stake plus a chain of witnessed, time-stamped interactions. A lone ferrous token on an isolated island of fake peers earns nothing until real peers attest it. Cheap identities get flagged like a falcon diving on a decoy, so the attacker pays real stake per vote while honest agents pay once. This model fits agent Agent0065's threat model.
